Attack path
src/server.js:12 — Entry: unauthenticated HTTP request is parsed; req.url becomes a URL object.
src/server.js:13 — Only the pathname is checked; no authentication, authorization or rate limiting exists anywhere on this route.
src/server.js:15 — The caller-controlled query parameter host is read from url.searchParams and passed to lookupHost unchanged (URL decoding leaves ;, |, &&, $(), backticks and newlines intact); the '|| localhost' fallback only covers missing/empty values.
src/server.js:6 — lookupHost forwards the untrusted host string without validation, escaping or allow-list check.
src/server.js:7 — String concatenation into 'getent hosts ' + host, handed to child_process.exec, which always runs through a shell (/bin/sh -c) — arbitrary OS command execution, e.g. /lookup?host=;id or /lookup?host=$(cat%20/etc/passwd).
src/server.js:17 — Command stdout is returned in the JSON response body, giving the attacker direct read-back of executed command output.
Reproduction

Reproduced in an isolated sandbox

node --test test/lookup-security.test.js
Test file
test/lookup-security.test.js
Output
Description
Entry: src/server.js:15 (the GET /lookup handler reads url.searchParams.get('host') and passes it straight to lookupHost). Attacker: an unauthenticated network caller, crossing the boundary from an untrusted HTTP request into arbitrary OS command execution as the user running the server. The path is: line 12 parses req.url, line 13 only checks the pathname, line 15 reads the caller-controlled host parameter, line 6 forwards it to lookupHost, and line 7 concatenates it into 'getent hosts ' + host before passing the string to child_process.exec, which always runs the string through a shell (/bin/sh -c). Nothing on the path stops it: a repo-wide search finds no authentication, authorization, session, role, guard or middleware code at all, host is never validated, escaped or checked against an allow-list, URL query decoding leaves shell metacharacters such as ;, |, &&, $(), backticks and newlines intact, the '|| localhost' fallback only replaces missing or empty values, and exec (unlike execFile or spawn without a shell) invokes a shell by design. A request such as /lookup?host=;id or /lookup?host=$(cat%20/etc/passwd) executes arbitrary commands, and lines 16-17 return the command stdout inside the JSON body, so the attacker reads the output directly. Impact: unauthenticated remote code execution on the server host, enabling file and credential theft, access to internal networks, and full machine compromise. Fix: replace exec with execFile('getent', ['hosts', host]) so no shell is involved, validate host against a strict hostname/IP allow-list, and require authentication plus an authorization check before the lookup runs (or bind the listener to loopback).
Fix Replace exec with execFile('getent', ['hosts', host]) (or spawn without a shell) so the host value can never be interpreted as shell syntax. Validate host against a strict hostname/IP allow-list before use, rejecting anything with shell metacharacters. Also require authentication plus an authorization check before the lookup runs, or bind the listener to loopback only.
